anomalies.observed: T3 is implemented as a P-channel device in a high-side position: T3 pin 2 (S) is on /+24V_F, T3 pin 3 (D) is on +24V, and T3 pin 1 (G) is self-biased through R7/D3 on /G_RPP. The ATO valve load is instead switched by T5 (AO3400A) on /G_ATO and /D_ATO.
anomalies.expected: The specification states T3 is an AON6407 N-MOSFET low-side switch that drives the ATO_VALVE load, with its gate driven through R10 and pre-driven by T4.

evidence.quote: T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch | Netlist: drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).

anomalies.impact: The board does not match the specified T3 role: T3 is a high-side P-channel switch in the main 24 V path rather than the specified low-side N-channel ATO switch. If the intended design was a GPIO-controlled low-side ATO switch at T3, the actual power path and switching behavior are different; the ATO valve is switched by T5 and the 24 V rail is gated by an uncontrolled high-side P-FET.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows T3 as a P-channel high-side switch on the 24 V rail, while the specification describes T3 as the N-channel low-side ATO-valve switch; this component-type/topology mismatch is the clearest deviation from the intended design.
